# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes #4694

## What does this PR do?
- Optimize indexes listings by not processing all indexes and only processing the ones that are used as the result of the pagination
- Don't open the index if they are already cached


## PR checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:
- [x] Does this PR fix an existing issue, or have you listed the changes applied in the PR description (and why they are needed)?
- [x] Have you read the contributing guidelines?
- [x] Have you made sure that the title is accurate and descriptive of the changes?

Thank you so much for contributing to Meilisearch!

issue_context.title: Meilisearch takes an eternity to answer to `GET /indexes` when there is a few thousands indexes and timeout
issue_context.body:
I made 8000 indexes and while I was pushing documents to them I tried to list the indexes. It timed out AND it stopped all requests from reaching the server for a good minute.
The indexing part also seems to have stopped.
Then, it came back to normal automatically.

**To Reproduce**
Run this script;
```rust
BASELINE=$RANDOM
echo "Sending repeated updates..."
LOREM="Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text of the printing and typesetting industry. Lorem Ipsum has been the industry's standard dummy text ever since the 1500s, when an unknown printer took a galley of type and scrambled it to make a type specimen book. It has survived not only five centuries, but also the leap into electronic typesetting, remaining essentially unchanged. It was popularised in the 1960s with the release of Letraset sheets containing Lorem Ipsum passages, and more recently with desktop publishing software like Aldus PageMaker including versions of Lorem Ipsum."
for i in {0..8}; do LOREM="$(echo "$i" | shasum) $LOREM $(echo "$LOREM" | shasum) $LOREM $(echo "$LOREM $i" | shasum)"; done
echo "With content as large as $(echo "${LOREM}" | wc -c)B"
for iteration in {0..100000};
do
  for index in {0..8000};
  do
    SHASUM=$(echo "$iteration" | shasum)$(echo "$iteration$index" | shasum)
    for pk in {0..100}; do
      echo "{ \"id\": \"${BASELINE}_${pk}\", \"doggo\": \"$iteration $LOREM $iteration\", \"bad for perf\": \"$SHASUM\" }" | mieli -i "$index" document add --async > /dev/null
    done
  done
done
```

And then while it indexes run `mieli indexes list`.

**Expected behavior**
It works

**Meilisearch version:**
v1.8.2

**Additional context**
It seems like the index scheduler is opening and closing all the indexes; it shouldn’t need to do that to list the indexes.
Also, the `stats` routes work, which is even stranger since it's doing way more work.

review_comments: Hey, I’m wondering, why are we not simply calling the `index_stats` directly on the index-name instead of doing the double iterator stuff you implemented 🤔

I’ll be honest, I’m not a fan of leaking the internal `Uuid`, that’s not really supposed to come out of the index-scheduler.
I think we should only return the index_name here since we don't need anything else outside of the index-scheduler.
Not a fan of this part but I don't see any other easy way to do it
I tried size_hint but it just show me a size of 0 in both way
Yes, lmdb doesn't give us the info and thus we can't expose it either in heed 😔
